title: Nondegenerate-chain decomposition of the bar latching object
statement:
Let $I$ be a small category, let $\mathcal M$ be a category with all small coproducts, and let $V:I\to\mathcal M$ be a functor. Use the simplex category $\Delta$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n\geq0$ and $j\in I$, put
$$S_nV(j)=\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j}V(i_0).$$
For an order-preserving surjection $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$, the map $S_aV(j)\to S_nV(j)$ repeats the vertices according to $\theta$, inserts identity internal arrows, retains the final arrow to $j$, and acts identically on each $V(i_0)$-label. Let $D_n$ have objects the proper surjections $\theta:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[a]$, $a<n$. A morphism $\theta\to\theta'$ is a surjection $\rho:[a']\twoheadrightarrow[a]$ satisfying $\theta=\rho\theta'$. Give it the diagram $\theta\mapsto S_aV(j)$, with arrow map given by insertion according to $\rho$. Its canonical cocone to $S_nV(j)$ is the degree-$n$ simplicial latching cocone.
This diagram has a colimit $L_nS(j)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The canonical map to $S_nV(j)$ identifies, up to canonical isomorphism, with the coproduct injection
$$\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j\,;\,\exists k<n:\,(i_k\to i_{k+1})=1}V(i_0)\ \longrightarrow\ \coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j}V(i_0).$$
In particular there is a canonical decomposition
$$S_nV(j)\cong L_nS(j)\amalg N_nV(j),\qquad N_nV(j)=\coprod_{i_0\to\cdots\to i_n\to j\,;\,\forall k<n:\,(i_k\to i_{k+1})\ne1}V(i_0).$$
Only the $n$ internal arrows are tested; the final arrow $i_n\to j$ may be an identity. These identifications commute with postcomposition in $j$ and natural transformations of $V$. For $n=0$, $D_n$ is empty and $L_0S(j)$ is initial. No model structure, cofibrancy, images, or monomorphism assumption on coproduct injections is required.
